question: Does a paired-evidence-selected luminance axis add held-cube capacity to one bounded cylindrical tone/chroma operator beyond a fixed neutral axis, independent RGB curves and wrong-axis controls while retaining analytical gamut safety and a positive local Jacobian?

primary_source.title: Perception-Inspired Color Space Design for Photo White Balance Editing

clean_room_scope.borrowed_idea_only: a learnable luminance axis can define a cylindrical luminance/chroma coordinate system
clean_room_scope.project_mechanism: paired build samples select one frozen positive RGB axis; a fixed analytical tone/chroma transform is reconstructed in RGB and executed through the existing per-pixel maximum safe residual scale

stop_rules: Do not alter axes, transform amplitudes, grids, baselines, metrics or gates after any score.
Failure closes this exact learnable-axis cylindrical representation without axis-bank, parameter, curve-degree or threshold rescue.
Pass establishes synthetic explicit-operator capacity and safety only; it does not identify a film stock, real photographic style, illuminant, camera or product transform.
A later photographic challenger must use independently frozen paired or display-proxy evidence and unchanged severe-artifact and preference gates.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic clean-room representation capacity and analytical gamut-safety evidence for a bounded explicit colour operator; not photographic quality, film/stock response, calibration or product promotion.
